brief.headline: Push for ₹290/KG on Electral sachets to match Shrinath and offer 15-day faster payment in exchange for a 10% price cut

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹290/KG for Electral laminates, matching Shrinath Roto Pack; saves ₹3.91 L/year
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹290.00/KG to Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd for identical Electral sachets (LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 07 and others). GLS charges ₹295.00/KG — a 1.7% gap that costs us ₹3.91 L/year extra. The market ask for pharma ORS sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), so ₹290 is fair and inside the band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (15 Days After Receipt instead of 30) in exchange for roughly a 10% price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹9.49 L of our cash, but they borrow money at about 10.96%, so every day earlier is worth that rate to them — a 15-day jump is worth roughly 0.45% per month or about 5.4% annualized to them, so ask for a 10% one-time cut to seal the deal

brief.financialLeverage: GLS made a loss in FY2024-25 (₹-23.68 Cr) and their Altman Z-score is 1.68 (grey zone — neither safe nor failing, but fragile). They owe 2.15x their own cash and keep -3.4% of every ₹100 they sell (similar firms keep 2.5%). We are only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so we're tiny to them — but they're fragile. Don't squeeze so hard that supply breaks; lead with the faster-payment swap and keep two backup converters ready (Huhtamaki and Constantia Parikh are already in our system or well-known). Their credit rating is IVR BBB- / Stable and they have severe legal cases, GST filing delays and EPF payment delays — so treat them as a short-term source and line up alternates now.

evidence.point: We pay Shrinath ₹290/KG for the same Electral sachets; GLS charges ₹295/KG
They are in the grey distress zone
They owe more than twice their own cash
We are a very small customer to them

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already a tiny FDC supplier — proven and scalable for laminate sachets (revenue ₹2758.00 Cr, health C 59/100)

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter doing pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source fit (revenue ₹222.04 Cr, health D 31/100)

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film substrate AND conversion — can second-source at scale (revenue ₹16492.00 Cr, health C 46/100)

risks: GLS is loss-making, in the grey distress zone and has severe legal cases, GST filing delays and EPF payment delays — pushing too hard on price could tip them over and kill our supply
We are only 0.33% of their revenue, so we have almost no clout — they won't bend just to keep us
Their money-health score is 2/10 and credit rating IVR BBB- / Stable — treat them as a short-term source and line up two alternates (Huhtamaki, Constantia) before the meeting

They already take 53d to pay their own suppliers (peers: 36d) and keep -3.4% profit (peers: 2.5%) — so cash is very tight; offer the faster-payment swap rather than a straight price cut, and frame it as helping them
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to match the ₹290 per kilo we pay Shrinath for these same Electral sachets, and in return we can move you to 15-day payment — that puts cash in your hands two weeks earlier.
